# [CS045] Security-Critical Error Ignored (security-err-ignored)

The error of a call whose failure leaves the program insecure is dropped.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-252](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/252.html) |
| **OWASP** | A10:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Only a short list of calls is checked: random reads (a failed crypto/rand.Read leaves a zero key), bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword (ignoring it accepts any password), TLS handshakes, certificate verification, permission and privilege changes, and rows.Err after iterating query results. Ignored errors of other calls are not reported.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
key := make([]byte, 32)
rand.Read(key)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
key := make([]byte, 32)
if _, err := rand.Read(key); err != nil {
	return nil, err
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [security-err-ignored]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    security-err-ignored: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore security-err-ignored -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** security-err-ignored
```
